Plot latents results

Source: R/additive-compare.R, R/additive-methods.R, R/compare-models.R, and 11 more
latents-plots.Rd

plot() draws any result of this package and returns a ggplot object, which can be printed, saved with ggplot2::ggsave() or restyled with + ggplot2::theme(). The plots of mixture regressions (for fits that classify persons, the "fitted" view only), pooled imputations and bootstrap tests are drawn when called, including inside loops, and their ggplot is returned invisibly.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'latents_family_enumeration'
plot(
  x,
  what = c("bic", "aic", "bic_individual"),
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  criterion = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa_additive'
plot(
  x,
  what = c("means", "variances", "intercepts"),
  level = 0.95,
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'latents_comparison'
plot(x, main = NULL, subtitle = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa_cross_level'
plot(
  x,
  what = c("profiles", "group_means", "composition"),
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa_bootstrap_lrt'
plot(x, main = NULL, subtitle = NULL, palette = NULL, style = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'latents_growth_mixture'
plot(
  x,
  what = c("trajectories", "individuals", "coefficients", "random", "classification",
    "posteriors"),
  time = NULL,
  facet = FALSE,
  persons = 12L,
  max_persons = 120L,
  spread = 0.8,
  level = 0.95,
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'latents_transition_enumeration'
plot(
  x,
  what = c("bic", "aic", "bic_individual"),
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  criterion = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa_lta'
plot(x, main = NULL, subtitle = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'latents_mixture_regression'
plot(
  x,
  what = NULL,
  predictor = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  facet = FALSE,
  persons = 12L,
  max_persons = 120L,
  ...
)

plot_profiles(
  x,
  statistic = c("mean", "median", "mode"),
  scale = c("raw", "standardized"),
  intervals = TRUE,
  labels = TRUE,
  data = NULL,
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  what = c("lines", "bars", "heatmap", "raincloud", "parallel", "pairs", "all")
)

plot_responses(
  x,
  category = "last",
  intervals = TRUE,
  labels = TRUE,
  data = NULL,
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL
)

plot_sequences(
  x,
  labels = TRUE,
  cell_labels = TRUE,
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL
)

plot_prevalence(x, labels = TRUE, main = NULL, subtitle = NULL)

plot_diagnostics(
  x,
  what = c("all", "sizes", "posteriors", "entropy", "avepp", "group_sizes",
    "group_posteriors", "group_entropy", "group_avepp"),
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL
)

plot_transitions(x, main = NULL, subtitle = NULL)

plot_tree(x, main = NULL, subtitle = NULL)

plot_selection(
  x,
  what = c("all", "deltas", "heatmap", "smallest", "trust", "diagnostics"),
  using = "bic_groups",
  cutoff = 0.8,
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa'
plot(
  x,
  what = c("profiles", "bars", "heatmap", "raincloud", "parallel", "pairs", "responses",
    "probabilities", "sequences", "sizes", "entropy", "posteriors", "avepp", "all"),
  data = NULL,
  scale = c("raw", "standardized"),
  category = "last",
  labels = TRUE,
  intervals = TRUE,
  cell_labels = TRUE,
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  statistic = c("mean", "median", "mode"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa_enumeration'
plot(
  x,
  what = c("aic", "bic_groups", "bic_individual", "icl_individual"),
  criterion = NULL,
  combine = TRUE,
  labels = TRUE,
  mark_minimum = TRUE,
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  cutoff = 0.8,
  using = "bic_groups",
  ...
)

plot_enumeration(
  x,
  what = c("aic", "bic_groups", "bic_individual", "icl_individual"),
  combine = TRUE,
  labels = TRUE,
  mark_minimum = TRUE,
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  cutoff = 0.8,
  using = "bic_groups"
)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa_covariates'
plot(
  x,
  what = c("profiles", "bars", "heatmap", "raincloud", "parallel", "pairs", "responses",
    "sequences", "sizes", "entropy", "posteriors", "avepp", "all"),
  data = NULL,
  scale = c("raw", "standardized"),
  category = "last",
  labels = TRUE,
  intervals = TRUE,
  cell_labels = TRUE,
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  statistic = c("mean", "median", "mode"),
  ...
)

plot_views()

# S3 method for class 'latents_pooled'
plot(
  x,
  what = c("profile", "group", "measurement"),
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  level = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa_transitions'
plot(
  x,
  what = c("transitions", "profiles", "bars", "heatmap", "responses", "sequences",
    "sizes", "entropy", "posteriors", "avepp", "all"),
  data = NULL,
  scale = c("raw", "standardized"),
  category = "last",
  labels = TRUE,
  cell_labels = TRUE,
  main = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  intervals = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

The object to plot: a profile, class or transition model for the named fit views and plot_diagnostics(); an enumeration from enumerate_classes(), enumerate_lpa() or enumerate_lca() for plot_enumeration(), plot_selection() and plot_tree(); a transition fit from lta() for plot_transitions(). A general lta() fit (occasion-varying transitions, covariates, mover-stayer, second order, weights, ordinal or count indicators) draws only its transition matrix, with plot_transitions() or plot(). Transition and group-class family grids plot with plot(x, what = ).

what

The view to draw. "all" draws every view of that function that the model supports, as a list, and names in a message any it cannot draw. For plot_profiles(): "lines" (default), "bars" (means from zero with 95% intervals), "heatmap" (means in observed standard deviations, or the response probabilities of categorical indicators), "raincloud" (each indicator's distribution by assigned profile), "parallel" (every case as a line) or "pairs" (scatter-plot matrix with each profile's 95% covariance ellipse).

For plot_diagnostics(): "all" (default), "sizes" (effective profile counts), "posteriors" (posterior probability of each case's assigned profile), "entropy" (each case's entropy relative to a flat posterior) or "avepp" (average posterior probability matrix). "group_sizes", "group_posteriors", "group_entropy" and "group_avepp" draw the same four views for the groups and their group classes; "all" includes them when the fit has two or more group classes, and with fewer they are refused with latents_no_group_classes. A fit with a noise component supports "sizes" and the group views only: "all" returns "sizes", and the other individual-level views are refused with latents_unsupported_noise.

For plot_selection(): "all" (default), "deltas", "heatmap", "smallest", "trust" or "diagnostics", as described for plot_enumeration().

For plot_enumeration(), three kinds of view; information criteria cannot be requested together with the other two:

  • Information criteria: criterion columns of as.data.frame(x), such as "bic_groups", or "all". The default draws AIC, both BICs and ICL over individuals.

  • Classification quality across the candidates, at each level with two or more classes: "entropy" (relative entropy), "avepp" (the lowest AvePP, with the cutoff dashed) or "diagnostics" (both).

  • Model-selection evidence (none of which selects a model): "deltas" (the decrease in the criterion in using with each added profile and each added group class; see get_results(x, "deltas") and "knees"), "heatmap" (the criterion over profiles and group classes, relative to the lowest), "smallest" (the smallest class share, with 5% dashed) or "trust" (convergence, boundary and replication of every candidate). "selection" draws all four and "diagnostics", as a list.

main, subtitle

Title and subtitle. NULL (default) uses the view's own.

criterion

The former name of what for enumeration criteria. On a profile grid it is used alone or with what = "enumeration"; transition and group-class family grids take "bic", "aic" or "bic_individual".

...

Not used. Profile, class and transition models and enumerations refuse unknown arguments with latents_bad_argument; the other methods ignore them with a latents_unused_argument warning (see Errors).

level

Confidence level for additive, mixture-regression and growth views (default 0.95). On pooled plots, the former name of what: "profile", "group" or "measurement".

palette

For bootstrap plots, a colour vector for the histogram and the observed statistic; NULL (default) uses the standard colours.

style

The former bootstrap drawing style; ignored with a latents_unused_argument warning.

time

For growth and trajectory views, the numeric time column. NULL (default) uses the first numeric variable in the fitted random or regression design.

facet

For trajectories, FALSE (default) draws all classes in one panel; TRUE draws one panel per class.

persons

For individual trajectories, the number of persons to show (default 12), or a vector of their identifiers.

max_persons

The maximum number of observed trajectories drawn behind the class means (default 120); zero hides them.

spread

For growth trajectories, the band of random-effect spread of persons around the class curve, from 0 (hidden) to less than 1; default 0.8.

predictor

For the fitted view of a mixture regression, a numeric predictor in the formula. NULL (default) uses the first numeric predictor.

statistic

"mean" (default), "median" or "mode". They coincide for continuous indicators; for categorical ones they summarise the fitted probabilities on the numeric category scale, without intervals.

scale

"raw" (default) keeps each indicator in its own units; "standardized" divides its deviation from the observed mean by its observed standard deviation.

intervals

For profile, bar and response views, TRUE (default) draws 95% intervals when the fit has standard errors; otherwise the subtitle states why there are none. They are the conf_low and conf_high of parameter_inference(); a response probability's interval is formed on the logit scale.

labels

TRUE (default) labels each series directly; FALSE uses a legend. On sequence views, TRUE groups the rows by group class under labelled strips.

data

The data the model was fitted to, used only to compute the intervals. NULL (default) uses the data stored in the fit.

category

Which category's probability to draw: "last" (default), "first", or a single label or index.

cell_labels

For sequence views, TRUE (default) prints each assigned profile in its cell when the cells are large enough for the text.

using

For plot_enumeration(what = "deltas"), "heatmap" or "selection", the information criterion used (default "bic_groups"); "smallest" and "trust" use none.

cutoff

For plot_enumeration(what = "avepp"), "diagnostics" or "selection", the AvePP cutoff drawn as a dashed line (default 0.8).

combine

TRUE (default) draws several criteria as panels of one plot; FALSE returns one plot per criterion.

mark_minimum

TRUE (default) circles each criterion's lowest value among converged candidates, without selecting a model. Information criteria only.

Value

A ggplot object. what = "all" (on plot() of a fitted model or on a named plot function), plot_enumeration(combine = FALSE) with several criteria or classification-quality measures, and enumeration views when more than one is requested (including "selection") return a latents_plots list of ggplot objects, which draws each one when printed. plot_views() returns a data.frame with one row per view: type (the value for what), group and description.

Details

The main views also have their own functions, each grouping related views under what, with "all" drawing every one: plot_profiles() (profile means as lines, bars, a heatmap, rainclouds, parallel lines or pairs, or categorical means, medians and modes), plot_responses() (categorical response probabilities), plot_sequences() (each group's profile at each occasion), plot_prevalence() (profile shares within each group class), plot_diagnostics() (classification quality), plot_transitions() (transition matrix), plot_enumeration() (information criteria, classification quality and model-selection evidence across a grid), plot_selection() (the model-selection evidence of a grid) and plot_tree() (how profiles split as more are added). Each draws the same plot as the matching plot(x, what = ). plot_views() lists the views of a fitted model, and "enumeration" and "tree" for a grid, with a one-line description of each; the other grid views are listed under what below.

Each profile keeps the same order (largest first), Okabe-Ito colour and point shape in every view. The plots require ggplot2, which is a suggested package.

What plot() draws

Each object takes what = for its views, main, subtitle and the arguments named here.

Fitted profile and class models

From multilpa(), multilca(), lpa(), lca() and covariate models: "profiles" (default), "bars", "heatmap", "raincloud", "parallel", "pairs" (each profile's 95% covariance ellipse), "responses", "probabilities" (not for covariate models), "sequences" (fits with time; cell_labels = TRUE prints the profile in each cell), "sizes", "entropy", "posteriors", "avepp" and "all". The profile views name in a caption any ordinal, count or (for the means) categorical indicator they omit.

Transition fits

From lta(): "transitions" (default), then "profiles", "bars", "heatmap", "responses", "sequences", "sizes", "entropy", "posteriors", "avepp" and "all", without statistic; the profile, bar and response views draw the 95% intervals of the transition fit's parameter_inference() (intervals). A general lta() fit takes no what and draws its transition matrix.

Enumerations

Criterion columns or "all" (with combine, labels and mark_minimum), "tree", the classification-quality views "entropy", "avepp" and "diagnostics" (with cutoff), and the model-selection views "deltas" and "heatmap" (which use the criterion in using), "smallest" and "trust"; "selection" draws those four and "diagnostics". Transition and group-class family grids take "bic" (default), "aic" or "bic_individual".

Additive fits

"means" (default; each group class's mean with its Wald interval), "variances" (within- and between-group variances) or "intercepts" (each group's posterior intercept); level sets the interval.

Cross-level fits

"profiles" (default), "group_means" or "composition" (profile shares within each group class).

Mixture regressions

"fitted" (default: the outcome against a numeric predictor, one line per class), "coefficients" or "posteriors"; level sets the intervals. Fits that classify persons (class_level = "group") default to "trajectories" (unless predictor is given) and also take "individuals" and "classification", as growth mixtures do.

Growth mixtures

"trajectories" (default: class mean trajectories with bands; facet, max_persons, spread), "individuals" (persons: a number or identifiers), "coefficients", "random" (predicted random effects with each class's 95% ellipse) or "classification" (also "posteriors"); time names the time variable, level the band.

Pooled imputations

"profile" (default), "group" or "measurement" parameters: each imputation's estimate beside the pooled one with its interval.

Model comparisons, bootstrap tests, diagnostics

One view each: the criteria of each compared model, the simulated null distribution with the observed statistic, and the views of plot_diagnostics().

Former argument names

Enumeration plots accept criterion (now what; on a profile grid what = "enumeration" is the default criteria view), pooled plots accept level (now what), and bootstrap plots accept palette (the histogram and observed-line colours). On an enumeration, criterion with any what other than "enumeration" is an error of class latents_bad_argument (with "tree", a warning, as the tree uses no criterion); level together with what on a pooled plot is an error of the same class.

Errors

latents_missing_package without ggplot2; latents_bad_argument for an argument the object's plot does not take, except that the plots of additive, cross-level, general transition (lta()), growth-mixture, mixture-regression, pooled, comparison and bootstrap results and of transition or group-class family grids ignore it with a latents_unused_argument warning (including a bootstrap plot's style); latents_bad_argument also when a named plot function is given an object it does not draw; latents_nothing_to_plot when the fit lacks what a view needs (for example posteriors or entropy of a one-profile fit, prevalence of a covariate model, or the case-level views of a centred fit); latents_unknown_category when category names no category of an indicator; latents_no_continuous, latents_no_categorical and latents_no_time when a view needs indicators or occasions the fit does not have; latents_unknown_criterion for a criterion not in the grid.

References

Satopaa, V., Albrecht, J., Irwin, D. and Raghavan, B. (2011). Finding a "kneedle" in a haystack: detecting knee points in system behavior. 31st International Conference on Distributed Computing Systems Workshops, 166-171.

Zappia, L. and Oshlack, A. (2018). Clustering trees: a visualization for evaluating clusterings at multiple resolutions. GigaScience, 7(7), giy083.

Examples

plot_views()
#>             type       group
#> 1       profiles measurement
#> 2           bars measurement
#> 3        heatmap measurement
#> 4      raincloud measurement
#> 5       parallel measurement
#> 6          pairs measurement
#> 7      responses measurement
#> 8  probabilities   structure
#> 9      sequences   structure
#> 10   transitions   structure
#> 11         sizes diagnostics
#> 12       entropy diagnostics
#> 13    posteriors diagnostics
#> 14         avepp diagnostics
#> 15   enumeration   selection
#> 16          tree   selection
#> 17           all       every
#>                                                                                       description
#> 1                         Profile means, medians or modes across indicators, one line per profile
#> 2                                     Profile means as grouped bars from zero, with 95% intervals
#> 3                            Profile means in observed standard deviations from the observed mean
#> 4                   Each indicator's distribution by assigned profile: density, box, observations
#> 5                                   Every case as a line across indicators, one panel per profile
#> 6                                  Scatter-plot matrix with each profile's 95% covariance ellipse
#> 7                                        Categorical response probabilities, one line per profile
#> 8                              Profile prevalence within each group class, the two-level quantity
#> 9                                        Each group's profile at each occasion, one row per group
#> 10                      Estimated transition matrix, one panel per group class (a transition fit)
#> 11                                      Effective number of cases in each profile, with its share
#> 12                                   Each case's entropy relative to a flat posterior, by profile
#> 13                              Posterior probability of each case's assigned profile, by profile
#> 14                           Average posterior probability: assigned profile by posterior profile
#> 15 Information criteria across a candidate grid (plot an enumeration; or name criteria in `what`)
#> 16                                     How profiles split as more are added (plot an enumeration)
#> 17                            Every view above that this fit has the ingredients for, in one call
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fit <- multilpa(course_engagement, c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read"),
                  "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2,
                  n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
  plot_profiles(fit)
  plot_diagnostics(fit, what = "avepp")
}
